observations: Photo 0 shows a DSLR-style camera body held in a hand, with 'Nikon' clearly printed on the pentaprism housing.
A lens is attached with a gold/bronze accent ring near the mount, consistent with some third-party lens lines (e.g. Sigma Art series), but no brand or model text is legible on the lens itself.
No visible proof of model number (D810), serial plate, screen-on condition, shutter count, or lens focal markings in the single photo provided.
Background is a plain indoor wall with a switch plate; no additional accessories (box, charger, strap, memory card) are shown.

claims.claim: Nikon D810 DSLR Camera + 24-70mm Lens for Sale
claims.evidence: Seller's own text later states 'The brand is Canon', directly conflicting with both the ad title and the visible 'Nikon' badge in photo 0.
No close-up of sensor, LCD screen, lens glass, or body wear is shown.
A lens is attached in photo 0, but no focal length or brand text is legible on it.

risks.risk: Brand/model identity conflict suggests a copy-pasted, mismatched, or deliberately confusing listing, a common precursor to scam sales.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the camera's top/front badge, model plate, and lens barrel text, plus a video showing the camera powering on.
risks.if_unproven: treated as a misrepresented or unverifiable listing, priced at worst case or rejected pending clarification

risks.risk: Unknown functional condition (shutter count, sensor, autofocus) since no power-on or sample image is shown.
risks.proof: Video of camera turning on, taking a test shot, and displaying shutter count via menu.

risks.risk: Lens identity and condition unconfirmed (could be a cheaper kit lens rather than a 24-70mm).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of lens barrel showing brand, focal length, and aperture markings.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unverified lens, not premium 24-70mm

proof_requests: Clear photo of the camera's top plate and model badge (to confirm D810 or actual model).
Close-up of the lens barrel showing brand and focal length markings.
Video of the camera powering on and displaying a sample shot or shutter count.
Photo of the serial number plate under the lens mount or battery compartment.
response.reason: The seller's text directly contradicts itself by naming the item a 'Nikon D810' while also stating 'The brand is Canon,' and this inconsistency is not resolved by the single photo, which shows a Nikon-badged body with an unidentified lens — a strong signal of a mismatched or deceptive listing.
